## For the curator

Climb batch 26 landed on 5 November and is pushed. It made four changes. The interpreter now accepts a program's own operators between an array and a number beside a vector's own operator, as the compiler's type checker already did; this is the first of the two steps of your decision on opening `Number`. The specification's overview of operators now says that a comparison with a NaN, or with the rational 0/0, answers false, as your decision on NaN comparisons asked. The compiler now compiles functions declared inside a block, which nine library functions needed, the sum operator's among them. And 18 more of the library's built-in functions, the string functions, now call Java methods that both the interpreter and the compiler can call, so 306 of the 449 do.

The full check of the merged tree was green, the compiler's type checker still finds no error in the library, and both quick microGPT checks passed 7 of 7. The run wrote 2.6 million tokens in under two and a half hours, against the plan's 3.6 million and four and a quarter hours. The two and a half days of work before the run wrote 16.3 million, 3.9 million of them for this batch's planning and reviews; about 1.4 million of that went on agents resumed after long waits, which had to reread their whole context.

One finding touches a decision of yours. Your decision on self-typed traits gave the compiler's type checker a rule that a type must be what it claims to be, and left the interpreter unchanged. The interpreter now reads such traits the way that rule allows, without checking the rule, so it accepts a wrongly declared type and then picks one of two matching functions. The default keeps the interpreter as it is, since the compiler refuses such a program; the other way adds the check to the interpreter.

The batch's choices taken without you are on your review list, each with a default that keeps what landed: the compiled local functions as their own objects, and the string functions' design at the reviewer's default. One question has no default: two system functions now call a Java class that the type checker cannot read with the interpreter's library, so they will fail when the checker first reads them; I suggest moving them to the Java class that the other string functions use.

Climb batch 26 landed on 5 November and is pushed. It made four changes.             if start.group(1):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""plan-moves.py --root WT --base AT [--stale-at REV]: check that every line taken out of PLAN.md went to PLAN-history.md word for word, and list the PLAN lines that look stale.

A line taken out is a line of PLAN.md at AT, the commit that the worktree WT was made at, that the working
PLAN.md no longer holds, as a whole line: a line moved, cut to a pointer, or changed. Each must stand among
the lines that the working PLAN-history.md gained since AT, as many times as it went. PLAN-history.md only
gains: a line that it lost is a failure too. Blank lines are not counted. Prints the counts, the headings
that PLAN-history.md gained, and each failure; exit 1 on any.

Then, for information only (they never fail), the PLAN lines to look at, one `LOOK` line each with its
reason, read against the working review queue and the history of AT:
  settled   a list line whose own pointer, a sentence "Review-queue item 296.", names items that are each
            settled in the queue's part (a), and that names no item open in (b) or (c)
  list      a list line that names three or more items, some of them settled; or one that ties its items
            to a list of the queue's head (the queue's "Needed before the switch-over") and does not name
            the same items
  finding   a line `- Climb batch N's review, finding M ...` whose finding a commit in the history of AT
            names (`batch-N-review.md, finding M`, or "climb batch N's finding M"), where that commit
            changes a file outside the record: a half of the line may be built
With --stale-at REV, it reads PLAN.md and the review queue at REV, and the history of REV, prints only the
LOOK lines, and exits 0: evidence.py gives them to the sorter in plan.md.
"""
import argparse
import collections
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument('--root', required=True)
ap.add_argument('--base', required=True)
ap.add_argument('--stale-at')
a = ap.parse_args()
D = 'explorations/coordinator/'


def at(rel, rev=None):
    rev = rev or a.base
    r = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', a.root, 'show', '%s:%s' % (rev, D + rel)], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode:
        sys.exit('plan-moves.py: no %s at %s' % (rel, rev))
    return r.stdout.split('\n')


def now(rel):
    with open(os.path.join(a.root, D + rel), encoding='utf-8') as f:
        return f.read().split('\n')


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the PLAN lines to look at

ITEMS = re.compile(r'[Rr]eview-queue items? (\d+(?:(?:,\s*|,? and |,? or )\d+)*)')
OWN = re.compile(r'(?:^\s*- |[.;]\s+)Review-queue items? (\d+(?:(?:,\s*|,? and |,? or )\d+)*)')
HEAD_LIST = re.compile(r'\*\*([^*]+?):\*\*\s*(\d[\d,\s]*)')
FINDING_LINE = re.compile(r"\s*- [Cc]limb batch (\w+)'s review, finding (\d+)\b")
RECORD = re.compile(r'explorations/(coordinator/(PLAN|PLAN-history|review-queue|INDEX|FACTS|POSITIONS|FACTS-history|POSITIONS-history|BOOT|HELD)\.md$|reviews/|fortress-gap-ledger)')


def queue_sets(lines):
    """(open, settled, heads): the item numbers open in (b) and (c), those settled in (a) and open nowhere,
    and each list of the queue's head that names its items by number, {label in lower case: numbers}."""
    part, opened, settled, heads = None, set(), set(), {}
    for ln in lines:
        if ln.startswith('## '):
            m = re.match(r'## \((\w)\)', ln)
            part = m.group(1) if m else ('after' if part else None)
            continue
        if part in ('b', 'c'):
            m = re.match(r'(\d+)\. ', ln)
            if m:
                opened.add(int(m.group(1)))
        elif part == 'a':
            m = re.match(r'- \*\*(?:Items? )?(\d+)[,.]', ln)
            if m:
                settled.add(int(m.group(1)))
        elif part is None:
            for m in HEAD_LIST.finditer(ln):
                heads[m.group(1).strip().lower()] = {int(x) for x in re.findall(r'\d+', m.group(2))}
    return opened, settled - opened, heads


def findings_built(rev):
    """{(batch, finding): [(hash, subject)]}: the review findings that a commit in rev's history names,
    for each commit that changes a file outside the record."""
    r = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', a.root, 'log', '--format=%x00%h%x01%s%x01%B%x01', '--name-only', rev],
                       capture_output=True, text=True)
    out = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for chunk in r.stdout.split('\x00')[1:]:
        h, s, body, files = chunk.split('\x01', 3)
        if not [f for f in files.split('\n') if f.strip() and not RECORD.match(f.strip())]:
            continue
        msg = s + '\n' + body
        named = set()
        for m in re.finditer(r'batch-(\w+)-review\.md,? findings? (\d+(?:(?:,\s*|,? and )\d+)*)', msg):
            named.update((m.group(1).lower(), int(n)) for n in re.findall(r'\d+', m.group(2)))
        for m in re.finditer(r"[Cc]limb batch (\w+)'s (?:review, |post-batch review, )?findings? (\d+(?:(?:,\s*|,? and )\d+)*)", msg):
            named.update((m.group(1).lower(), int(n)) for n in re.findall(r'\d+', m.group(2)))
        for k in named:
            out[k].append((h, s))
    return out


def stale(plan, queue, rev):
    """The LOOK lines of PLAN's lines against the queue and the history of rev."""
    opened, settled, heads = queue_sets(queue)
    built = findings_built(rev)
    out, h2, h3 = [], None, None
    for i, ln in enumerate(plan, 1):
        if ln.startswith('## '):
            h2, h3 = ln[3:].strip(), None
            continue
        if ln.startswith('### '):
            h3 = ln[4:].strip()
            continue
        if not ln.lstrip().startswith('- '):
            continue
        why = []
        nums = []
        for m in ITEMS.finditer(ln):
            nums += [int(x) for x in re.findall(r'\d+', m.group(1))]
        own = [int(x) for m in OWN.finditer(ln) for x in re.findall(r'\d+', m.group(1))]
        s = sorted({n for n in nums if n in settled})
        if own and all(n in settled for n in own) and not any(n in opened for n in nums):
            why.append('settled: its own review-queue item is in (a): %s' % ', '.join(map(str, sorted(set(own)))))
        elif s and len(set(nums)) >= 3:
            why.append('list: it names items in (a) among open ones: %s' % ', '.join(map(str, s)))
        q = re.search(r"the queue's \"([^\"]+)\"", ln)
        if q and q.group(1).strip().lower() in heads:
            want, got = heads[q.group(1).strip().lower()], set(nums)
            if want != got:
                diff = (['it names %s, which the queue\'s list does not' % ', '.join(map(str, sorted(got - want)))] if got - want else []) + \
                       (['it lacks %s, which the queue\'s list holds' % ', '.join(map(str, sorted(want - got)))] if want - got else [])
                why.append('list: against the queue\'s "%s", %s' % (q.group(1), ', and '.join(diff)))
        f = FINDING_LINE.match(ln)
        if f and (f.group(1).lower(), int(f.group(2))) in built:
            cs = built[(f.group(1).lower(), int(f.group(2)))]
            why.append('finding: %s names this finding: %s' % ('a commit' if len(cs) == 1 else '%d commits' % len(cs),
                                                               '; '.join('%s "%s"' % (h, sub[:90]) for h, sub in cs[:3])))
        if why:
            out.append('LOOK PLAN.md:%d, under "%s": %s. The line: %s' % (i, h3 or h2, '; '.join(why), ln.strip()[:160]))
    return out


if a.stale_at:
    looks = stale(at('PLAN.md', a.stale_at), at('review-queue.md', a.stale_at), a.stale_at)
    print('\n'.join(looks) if looks else 'None.')
    sys.exit(0)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the moves, word for word

plan0, plan1 = at('PLAN.md'), now('PLAN.md')
hist0, hist1 = collections.Counter(at('PLAN-history.md')), collections.Counter(now('PLAN-history.md'))
out = [l for l in (collections.Counter(plan0) - collections.Counter(plan1)).elements() if l.strip()]
gained = hist1 - hist0
lost = [l for l in (hist0 - hist1).elements() if l.strip()]
first = {}
for i, l in enumerate(plan0, 1):
    first.setdefault(l, i)
missing = []
for l in out:
    if gained[l] > 0:
        gained[l] -= 1
    else:
        missing.append(l)
heads = [l for l in (hist1 - hist0).elements() if l.startswith('#')]
print('plan-moves: %d lines taken out of PLAN.md; PLAN-history.md gained %d lines, under %d headings' % (
    len(out), sum(1 for l in (hist1 - hist0).elements() if l.strip()), len(heads)))
for h in heads:
    print('  gained heading: %s' % h)
for l in missing:
    print('FAIL not in PLAN-history.md word for word: PLAN.md:%d at %s: %s' % (first.get(l, 0), a.base, l[:160]))
for l in lost:
    print('FAIL PLAN-history.md lost a line: %s' % l[:160])
looks = stale(plan1, now('review-queue.md'), a.base)
for l in looks:
    print(l)
print('plan-moves: %s; %d PLAN lines to look at' % ('pass' if not missing and not lost else '%d failures' % (len(missing) + len(lost)), len(looks)))
sys.exit(1 if missing or lost else 0)

1	<!-- The record-landing workflow's routing writer brief: after a batch's landing, bring PLAN, PLAN-history, the review queue, INDEX and other notes in line with it in the run's worktree, as the sort assigned, with each moved line word for word; and fix them once from the checks. -->
2	
3	# The routing writer of the record-landing workflow
4	
5	You are a stream writer in the Fortress revival repository: a headless Opus session that takes its tasks one after another. Your standing order is the skill writer's, in your first message: its register and its writing principles hold. Its parts on skill files, on committing and on `sources.md` do not: you edit record files in the worktree, and you commit nothing. Your task names the batch, the run's folder and the worktree. The worktree is this run's own checkout, and your session runs in it: every path here is from the worktree's root.
6	
7	The curator is the person in charge of the project. PLAN (`explorations/coordinator/PLAN.md`) is the working plan: its phases, the curator's answers in the order the work needs them, and the parked items. `PLAN-history.md` holds, word for word, each line taken out of PLAN, under a heading for the landing that moved it. The review queue (`review-queue.md`) is the one home of each item that waits for the curator's word or review, numbered, in three parts: (b) consequential, (c) routine, (a) settled or stale. `INDEX.md` holds one line for each note. A landing is the commit that put a batch's merged work on `main`. An entry is one line of FACTS or POSITIONS under its permanent number.
8	
9	## The problem
10	
11	A batch has landed. PLAN still says where the work stood before it: its "Where we stand", the batch's own line in its phase, lines that the batch built or answered, and lines that no longer hold. The batch's items for the curator wait in PLAN's list for his review, or in no file. The review queue's head names the old next batch. Notes have no INDEX line. A sorter has listed what the record owes, one change per line, in `owed.md` in the run's folder. Each change has a number (C1, C2 ...), a home, a kind, a weight and its ground. Your homes are five: a PLAN line, PLAN-history, a review-queue item, an INDEX line, and a line of another note. The entries writer takes FACTS, POSITIONS, their histories and the gap ledger at the same time, in the same worktree.
12	
13	## The question
14	
15	For each change of `owed.md` whose writer is `routing`, what do PLAN, PLAN-history, the queue, INDEX or the note hold after it? Make the edit in the worktree, so that each file stands in line with the landing and nothing that it held is lost.
16	
17	## Where the sources are
18	
19	- `owed.md`, and the evidence beside it: `plan.md` (PLAN's headings with their lines, the lines that the batch added, and the other lines that name a changed entry or row), `cites.md` (the queue items and INDEX lines that name them), `rows.md`, `checks.md` (the notes without an INDEX line, and the citations of PLAN by line number) and `sources.md` (the queries of the post-batch review's routing part and of the batch record's items for the curator).
20	- The routing's rule: `facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md#After the landing'`, its step 2.
21	- The form of a queue item: read the queue's head and three items of one of its themes (`facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/coordinator/review-queue.md#When each item is needed'`, and a theme's section).
